utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will slow down. Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The first thing I think we should deal with is associated exhibits, leftovers of yesterday. I see Ms. Marcus is hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I could request that we do something else first it would be -- Ms. Hochhauser is involved in a training and I was able to bring her in for an hour and a half this morning to deal with the witness. If that doesn't upset the Court schedule, I would appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't upset us at all. The Chamber wonders what Ms. Hochhauser needs to be trained in anymore, but apart from that, we have no objections. You would then examine the first witness. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. The witness being Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. As Mr. Hogan is being brought in, I would just point out the obvious, that there are some blow-ups of maps that the Prosecution intends to use. I've asked Mr. Lukic if he objects. He does not object to the use of the larger maps. So with the Court's permission, we'll use those as demonstrative exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the parties agree on this, then no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan. Before you give evidence, or before you continue to give evidence, I think it would be wise to ask you to make the solemn declaration again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hogan. Please be seated. Mr. Hogan, the Chamber understands that you're recalled as a consequence of an earlier decision of the Appeals Chamber which may have caused some gaps in the presentation of the evidence for the Prosecution. That's the reason why you are back in court. At least if we understand the Prosecution well. Ms. Hochhauser will further examine you. Ms. Hochhauser, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we could start, please, with 65 ter 19661 on the screen. Further Examination by Ms. Hochhauser:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us what it is that we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a map created by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I believe this is from July of 1992, and it came into the possession of the OTP in the year 2000, during a search of the ABiH archives by another OTP team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is -- is what we see on the map the -- I'm sorry, on the screen, the actual form in which it was recovered, so with these white text boxes as well?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the way it was recovered from the archives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you had an opportunity to look -- actually, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: First I'll tender the map. I'd like to tender at this point, Your Honours, 19661 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 19661 receives number P2951, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, in the absence of any objections, is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, have you had an opportunity to look at the confrontation lines in and around Sarajevo as drawn on this map, which is now in evidence as P2951, and to compare them with other maps indicating the same -- depicting the geographic region from this time-period, including SRK maps such as the one that are in the Sarajevo map book, P3?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. They might not be dated exactly the same date, the 2nd of July, 1992, but from the same general time-frame, I have compared these lines with the SRK lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And what was the result of that comparison?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: They were very -- very similar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now, if we could for a moment, please, have 65 ter 0828 -- sorry, 08282B, like boy, on the monitor, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, again, can you please tell us what it is that we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: This is another map of Sarajevo, showing confrontation lines. This is from -- created by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the year 1995, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know anything about how it came to be in the possession of the ICTY, or the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. In the spring of 2006, I made a request to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina for maps of this time-period, and this was physically brought to the Tribunal here in The Hague by General V Vahid Karavelic when he came for an interview, and I think it was June 2006.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender now, at this stage, 65 ter 08282B into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 08282B receives number P2952, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2952 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, have you had the opportunity to look at the lines, the confrontation lines as drawn on P2952, the map that remains on the monitor, and to compare the lines as depicted here on this BiH map with other maps showing the confrontation lines from this time-period, including the SRK maps contained in P003? And, if so, can you tell us the consult of that comparison or observation?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I have made such a comparison. And, again, the lines are similar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, regarding both of these maps, 2951 and 2952, did you provide today for us blow-up mounted copies in the original map size for the Chamber to view?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. These are -- first one we see here was the original size that was seized from the archives in 2000.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: With the -- with the permission of the Chamber if the witness could stand and show us the other one briefly? Or if the usher could. Either one. I think -- it's up to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever is practical, the Chamber always agrees.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I think the witness is comfortable doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As long as the witness-stand, he may be too far away from the microphone to be heard. So we should keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I first ask whether this is -- one second. Is this audible for the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Nobody is speaking right now, Mr. President. No --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but Mr. Hogan was speaking a minute ago. Could we first try to see whether we either have a movable microphone or whether to adjust the microphone in such a way that Mr. Hogan, if he speaks into the microphone, will be able to be heard. Mr. Hogan, could we do a test. Could you just say a few words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. As I say, this -- [B/C/S on English channel].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I -- I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm getting the translation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which suggests that at least something is heard to be translated. Could I seek confirmation from the English booth, I'm at this moment on the English channel, that Mr. Hogan can be heard. Could you speak a few words again, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I hope that the English booth can hear me now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters can hear the witness, but we fear that at some time he will turn his back on the microphones and that will change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, there is some fear that you'll turn your back to the microphones. Is -- don't we have any -- don't we have any -- one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Could I suggest maybe we move the easel closer to the witness instead of the witness closer to the easel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We took several actions. The first is that we ask Mr. Hogan perhaps to be as close to the microphone. Being seated diminishes any risk of not being heard. At the same time I asked whether someone could bring us a microphone which allows the speaking persons to move. Mr. Hogan. First question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So I -- I believe the -- the map is on -- displayed on top, which everybody can see now, is Exhibit Number P2951. Can you just orient us on that map to what we're looking at and what's indicated in terms of the confrontation lines and colours.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Hochhauser, we don't have it on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. I apologise, Your Honour. If we could also --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm trying. Sorry. I apologise. If we could also see it on the screen, please. It's 2951, Exhibit 2951.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the electronic image of the map that we see on the easel in front of us in the courtroom and this depicts the city of Sarajevo with red lines indicating the outline of the confrontation lines. In this particular map, there are only -- the only confrontation lines are indicated in red, without different lines for the opposing forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the map so that we can see red lines.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we orient ourselves to this feature, there central feature, which is Hum -- I'm sorry, Zuc, we can see a red line running diagonally across that feature which indicates a confrontation line, continues along the northern edge of the city, projects out towards the east before moving south again, and then along the southern edge to Grbavica, and then down towards the airport.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now if we could please see 2952, both in the hard -- the blow-up and also on the monitor, please. And if on the monitor we could similarly zoom in on the same portion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Hogan, can you please do the same thing with this map, just orient us to the confrontation lines and the colours used.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. In this particular map, the confrontation lines are drawn in two colours: Blue, to indicate forces of the ABiH; and red to indicate forces of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, or the VRS. Again, if we start at the north-west of the city, when the parties have time to compare the two maps side by side, you might notice that this line has been expanded a little bit towards the north-west, which indicates that the -- that the lines, confrontation lines moved slightly up towards Vogosca, again towards the east --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, it is perhaps not easy to follow if you don't see what you're doing. What you pointed at is that the feature which you, I think, called Zuc hill before, which was more or less divided by the line in two portions, seems now to be within the Federation-controlled area, at least most part of it. And in that context, you talked about the confrontation lines having moved to the north-west. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And you might observe also that towards the far east of the city, the lines have expanded further to the east so that the sort of peninsula that we noticed on the previous map has now flattened out a little bit farther to the east. And as we move south --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. Can you tell us what name that geographic area would have, if you're able?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: It's east of Vasin Han. I think it is Butila area. I would have to reorient myself with a blow-up of the map. But as we go south again towards Trebevic, which I'll point at the south-eastern part of the city, you'll notice that the lines have not changed noticeably. And coming west again, we can see that the lines around Grbavica are largely the same and then running down to the airport again. There is one change to the west that will you notice, that the lines moved to encompass Otes which is here. In the previous map we saw that the confrontation lines ran further to the west. Now these confrontation lines are easterly of Otes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask for one clarification at this moment. You talked about the peninsula which was flattened out. Now, if I compare the two maps, it seems that the peninsula which was on P2951, stretching a little bit into Serb-controlled area, it is not that that peninsula now seems to be -- have become Serb controlled, but, rather, that the surroundings of the peninsula apparently are depicted as having come under Federation control. So the flattening out did not exist in cutting off the peninsula but rather to widen the area around the original peninsula. Is that correctly -- is that a correct interpretation of what we see on this maps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hogan, can you tell us, the changes that you've just described in the confrontation lines in -- in and around Sarajevo as reflected in these two maps from July 1992 to March 1995, is that consistent with the -- essentially the fluctuations in the confrontation lines in this area throughout that period. So by looking at these two maps, do we get a sense of the whole picture of -- of the -- of the change in the confrontation lines from 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Essentially, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So can you point -- I'm now going to ask you some about some specific geographic regions. Can you point out to us, please, on this same exhibit, 2952, the elevations, and I'll go through a series of them, known as Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. Debelo Brdo is located approximately here. And if I could explain --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: -- in words. It is just to the north-west of Trebevic, within the ABiH line marked in blue, just as the line turns directly north towards -- to -- to encompass Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And actually, on these maps, if we were to zoom in sufficiently or look closely at these blow-ups are these elevations noted?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we say that it's approximately where it is written on the map "1.MB," that that's where Debelo Brdo is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think if you look at the brigade or the -- yes, the brigade marking, that notes "3.MB" correctly north of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think I missed it. Yes. From a distance, the 3, I mistook it for a 1. The -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Actually, it occurs to me that perhaps it would assist if could you mark it on the electronic version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that would be a good idea. Yes, could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, actually, before you mark, if it would assist you if we zoomed in at all, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because we can't zoom in any further once you started marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I think this is as good as it's going to get because the -- I think with this image we're going to lose resolution if we zoom in further. But can I mark it here. Approximately here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can I ask you, please, to do the same with, sorry, Colina Kapa?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness add DB to Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And similarly mark it with its initials, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mojmilo hill.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think we'll have to go a little bit further west on this image to see Mojmilo clearly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll -- we won't be able -- we can't move the image once it's -- so we'll hold off on that. You've already described to us the area of Zuc?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Mm-hm. And that would be up in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And also Hum.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That's my attempt at an H.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us, is it correct these are all elevations, they're all hills?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in whose territory were these hills?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: In the -- in the territory controlled by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether there were SRK positions that overlooked these hills?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: With the exception of Zuc, yes. All of these locations were overlooked by SRK positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender the marked map so we can -- at this point so we can keep going back to the unmarked one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, before we do so, you asked, although it is not marked, about Mojmilo hill. Was Mojmilo hill also controlled by Federation troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then map marked by the witness would receive what number, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P2953, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. One further question. Zuc hill, you marked it, you said it was under the control of the Federation. That is in this time-frame, 1995, because earlier you explained to us that Zuc hill was divided at an earlier point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'm marking it as depicted on it this map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and as you say, it was changing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's clear to me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you -- oh.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I can ask -- may I, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I was just checking whether it was admitted. It is. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Two follow-up questions, actually. For Mojmilo hill, can you tell us was that also overlooked by SRK territory?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: From the heights of Ozrenska Street area it overlooked Mojmilo hill. But to the west and south, it was not overlooked by SRK positions. And I should say Ozrenska Street was to the east of Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you also tell us, if you're able, when -- when the change that you just discussed with the Chamber in the previous exchange to Zuc hill occurred. So when did the change in that confrontation line happen, if you know.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: From the information that I was able to learn over the years, I believe it was in the autumn of 1992 or early spring of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please now go back to Exhibit 2951, both on the monitor and, I apologise, also on the hard copy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, can you please point to us, and if you -- if it would assist, which I'm going to guess it will, to zoom in on a portion of the map, if you could just tell us -- guide us in which -- how to zoom it in, the neighbourhood of Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the central part of the city, first of all. I think this is sufficient. And do you wish me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please. And if you could also just point it out on the big map.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: All right. On the big map, Hrasno is here, just to the west -- sorry. West of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness marked it as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And I'll mark this with an H.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about Hrasno hill? Is that ...

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: On the big map, Hrasno Brdo is just to the south of Hrasno. And I'll mark that on the electronic version.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With an HH. Or H ... Can you tell us in whose control was the area -- where the areas of Hrasno and Hrasno Brdo or Hrasno hill?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: They were in the area of control of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that change between 1992 and 1995, and when I say that I'm asking with reference to these maps, 2951 and 2952?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, it did not change.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned earlier in your testimony today when drawing a distinction about -- about confrontation lines, the Ozrenska Street. Ozrenska Street was the alleged origin of fire in the shooting -- in the sniping incident F4. And can you tell us where does Ozrenska Street fall in relation to Hrasno and Hrasno hill? Can you show that to us or describe it to us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, it's my recollection that the witness mentioned Ozrenska Street when he explained to us from what positions one could overlook Mojmilo hill rather than about any change in confrontation lines. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That's when I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said from the east Ozrenska Street, from there you could overlook it but not from other directions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I apologise for the unintentional mischaracterization, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But coming back to Ozrenska Street, since you did mention it and it does relate to F4, can you tell us what its relationship to Hrasno and Hrasno hill are?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, Ozrenska Street runs above Hrasno Brdo and Hrasno, and it's situated to the south of each. And I can point it out on the map and on the electronic version if you wish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would do it by a line and perhaps with arrows at both sides so that the line distinguishes from any confrontation lines we see there, whereas the colour is red always.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the big map, Ozrenska runs -- actually was the confrontation line - sorry - along this south -- southern edge. And on the electronic version, I'm drawing a line with an arrow at each end just to the north of the confrontation line. And as I say, the -- the street was the actual confrontation line on the southern edge above Hrasno and Hrasno Brdo. And I'm sorry, I didn't extend it far enough to the east because it would interfere with the circle and the letters that I've drawn, but it ran above Hrasno hill, Hrasno Brdo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn your attention --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Well, can I tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document P2951 as marked by the witness receives number P2954, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Ms. Hochhauser, at any suitable point in time, the Chamber sees that there are also a lot of blue markings which, at first sight, appear to be indications of military installations of the opposing party. But it also sees a lot of black markings, especially in the centre of town. If the witness later could explain what these stand for and whether he could confirm that the blue markings are markings depicting military items.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If it is acceptable to the Court, I'll turn to that at the end -- at the tail-end of the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I left it to you when to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn for a moment, please, to Mount Trebevic and still using Exhibit P2951, which is the 1992 confrontation line, can you show us, please, on this map -- can you orient us to the confrontation line in -- in -- around near Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. I'll show you on the big map first. The confrontation line ran along the Pale road which was situated on the northern and eastern shoulder of Mount Trebevic, here. And on the electronic map, if you would -- it's going to be difficult.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can zoom before you mark it if that's of assistance.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: It might be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we zoom in on the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On this map, the Pale road, if I could mark -- sorry. This is not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He needs the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we need to zoom in further or is this --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I think this will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'll mark the Pale road which runs here. And I'll draw an arrow at each end of it to indicate a line as opposed to the road. And I'll put a P next to that. And everything below and to the right of this line -- or -- and south and east of this line indicating the road is Month Trebevic. If you'll notice the very twisted road that runs near the letter P that I've marked, that road actually runs up the central spine of the mountain, of Mount Trebevic, and rises in height a great deal. The confrontation line, as you can notice on this map, was to the north of Trebevic and -- and the Pale road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just am looking at the transcript and it says and everything below and to the right of this line and then we lost you. So could you just repeat below and to the right of the line is what, and above and to the left of the line is what?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. The confrontation -- the line which I've indicated as the Pale road and marked with a letter P runs along the northern shoulder and -- northern and eastern shoulder of Trebevic. Everything to the south and east -- south-east of the Pale road line is Mount Trebevic. And the -- the twisted -- twisty road that can you see marked on this map near the letter P is a road which runs up the central spine of the mountain and rises in height a great deal. The -- and the confrontation line as can you see marked on this map in red to the north of the Pale road is -- is as it was depicted at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So by going up Trebevic from the Pale road, is that SRK territory?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below the Pale road going -- it would be down Trebevic, is that BiH territory?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether that remains the same on the 19 -- as depicted on the 1995 map, which is in evidence as 2952 now. Do these lines on Trebevic remain the same throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: With a slight variation. They -- the ABiH did push a little bit farther south that so that their lines reached just below -- 100, 200 metres just below the Pale road, so they did push a little bit farther, but by and large it was -- it was very similar. And Trebevic continually remained within SRK control.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I might, I'd like to tender this exhibit now, please, the marked exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number P2955, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now staying with this exhibit, 2951, and again if you'd need to -- need it to be zoomed in, please, just ask for that. I'd like to draw your attention to the Nedzarici neighbourhood. Are you familiar with what that neighbourhood looked like during the conflict period?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you please show us, both again on the large map and marking on the -- on the map on the monitor, just point out where the Nedzarici neighbourhood is and also specifically can you point out the salient in the confrontation line in Nedzarici so -- by which I mean the position that projected -- of one army into the other's territory?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. On the big map, this area is Nedzarici, sorry. And on the electronic version, I'll circle it -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The usher may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And mark it with an N. The area that looks like -- almost like a thumb protruding into the -- towards the city is the salient and it includes Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And under whose control was that salient?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: That was SRK control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us specifically about the salient, not the entire neighbourhood of Nedzarici but specifically the salient, can you describe the types of buildings in terms of their height that existed within that specific geographic area?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Largely, they were low apartment buildings, single-family houses. There was an army barracks. I think the highest building was the institute -- sorry. The Theological Institute which I believe was five or six storeys. But mostly they were two-to three-storey buildings in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Map marked by the witness receives number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number P2956, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hogan, I would like to turn briefly to the neighbourhood -- to the settlements of Dobrinja. And, actually, I'll leave to you whether you think 2951 or 2952 is the most -- would facilitate your showing this area the best.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I think the other map would be more appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could please go back to P2952. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As that's coming up, the Dobrinja settlements are often referred to with numbers. Can you just describe and explain that area.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. There was, as you say, Dobrinja 1 through Dobrinja 6, I think, and as well as the -- an area that was called the airport settlement. They were -- they were built at different times which is why they were numbered differently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you please --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I think we're going to need to zoom in on this map again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: More?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: If we can shift it down further so we can see a little bit farther south. There, that's it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you show us, please, and mark on the map the various areas of Dobrinja and how they were separated in terms of the confrontation line that ran through them.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: On the big map first, as you can see, the confrontation line at the south-east part of the -- of the settlement, ran between apartment buildings. And Dobrinja 1 and 4 were at the south -- furthest south-east area, and they came within the SRK lines. The remainder, except for the airport settlement, were within the ABiH lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you mark that on the -- on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The usher should assist first because the picture was moved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right. I'm always confused about which is Dobrinja 1 and which is Dobrinja 4. It is either 1 or 4, these ... and I'll mark them 1 and 4. If that's acceptable.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And those are 1 and 4 on this -- in control of the same warring party; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. And this is the airport settlement. And if you'll notice on the previous map, the 1992 map, the airport settlement was within the ABiH lines, and during the war it was -- the confrontation line moved so that it came under SRK control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: May I tender this exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document as marked by the witness receives number P2957, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. On the other map, Mr. Hogan, is it true that we do not see yet the fully constructed Dobrinja area, the 1992 map? Because I see some differences in what seems to be constructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That was going to be my next question, Your Honour, and I think it would actually assist if we could look at -- go back, and I apologise to the --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: -- to everybody else in the courtroom who has to deal with the switching back and forth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's correct. There is one part of Dobrinja that's not shown on this 1992 map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean a part which was a built-up area already but not being shown as such on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Has the -- has the confrontation -- the location of the confrontation line changed during that time-period though? From -- between 1992 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just explain that change.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. First of all, I should indicate this -- this area, which is -- which was constructed and not shown on this map, and this airport settlement which was -- where the confrontation line moved, and if I could mark it on this map that we see in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we should then zoom in on quite some detail to the airport area. Is this good enough, Mr. Hogan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This -- this is fine. And that is the airport settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the move of the confrontation line was that it became part of Serb-controlled area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If we could tender this map, please, this marked map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number with the marking of the airport settlement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number P2958, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to turn to the topic that you raised earlier about the markings on the map. I will say that before -- that I wanted to inform the Chamber in any case that we've located a -- it's called the instruction on working maps in the armed forces from the JNA. It's a document that has the symbols used and their and the explanation of the symbol used, and Mr. Lukic and I have been in conversation about what portions of that we might be able to agree to tender to Your Honours. So I just wanted you to be aware that that is in the works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any case, Mr. Hogan, if you can look at the exhibit that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser, at the same time, I am looking at the clock. I know what your plans are by now. You -- your estimate was half an hour. We are well beyond that. Now, how much time would you still need? Should we take a break now first and --

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: My only -- I'm done, Your Honour. Just to address the question that you raised, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest we deal with it and take the break after it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard His Honour's question but I'll -- just to put it back in the record next to the answer, can you tell us, looking at exhibit -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 2951, we see both blue and black, what appear to originally have been ink markings, can you tell us something about those?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The blue ink markings depicted in SRK territory show -- they are symbols for weapons, from -- anything from machine-guns to tanks to Howitzers. And I am familiar with some of them but I'm not an expert in testifying about what they represent. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you mark them, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I couldn't hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you please mark them on this map here. Let's see what is it that is referred to as ink markings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For example, I'll circle a few down here but they pretty much surround the city. All these ink markings surround the city. And if I could just demonstrate, some of them there would be a semi-circle with lines -- oops, lines running out from it. That would be one of the -- one of the symbols. For example, that is -- that is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us about the black versus blue ink. Is there any meaning to that?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The black that you see within the city, that's actually just a poor representation on this electronic version. It's -- if you have a close look at the -- at the full-sized map, that's just representing the city streets and city buildings. That's contained on the map. They're not hand-drawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the text boxes, are those -- what's the relationship between the text boxes and the markings? Are -- is there?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The text boxes were placed on that map by the ABiH officer who -- or intelligence, whoever prepared that map, to indicate certain information about weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, thank you for your patience. That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that you want to tender the marked version now marking the blue ink markings and the explanation the centre in red.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document marked by the witness receives number P2959, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. We'll take a break, after the witness has been escorted out of the courtroom. Mr. Hogan, we'd like to see you back in approximately 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And if there would be a possibility to have 2951, not electronically, but the hard copy be moved out of the courtroom so that I could have a closer look to it, and my colleagues as well, that would be appreciated. We will wait outside the courtroom. We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Lukic, we have a mobile microphone now for the witness. At the same time, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I used the wrong word. We have a microphone which allows the witness to move if he wishes to. At the same time, the Chamber considers that it's often more assisted by the markings on the map, rather than by gestures to a map, which may be difficult to decipher later for those reading the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Lukic. I think I explained to you before that Mr. Lukic is counsel for Mr. Mladic. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My cross won't be long.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to call P2951. Actually, it is on our screens, and it's the map on the stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 4 of temporary transcript, line 3, you said that you compared those maps and confrontation lines with maps of SRK. So can you tell us now where can we find those maps; and can you tell us ERN numbers or whatever you -- you know. So the maps you compared with those AB and H maps.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, in fact, some of them are included in the Sarajevo court binder which the Prosecution, I believe, has already tendered in this case. And I obtained additional maps besides the ones which were -- which were included in that court binder from the SRK archives in Banja Luka in 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said it's similar. So it's not the same. Can you tell us where the differences are, major differences at least?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- the SRK maps that I examined or compared tended to be of a larger scale. In other words, they did not only have a map of Sarajevo as we've seen in these two examples today. They had a larger area, which included the SRK zone of responsibility. Therefore, the -- the -- the lines that were drawn on such maps tended to be of a larger scale as well, so that when you zoom in on the city, the -- the lines would appear to be 2 to 300 metres wide, just the ink on the lines would appear to be 200 metres wide. So it is very hard to see when we know that confrontation lines ran from one side of the street to the other, to see that the line spreads out over such a large area, it's hard to be precise. That's why I say they were similar, not exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. On page 4, lines 11 to 16 of today's temporary transcript, you said that in -- in spring of 2006, you asked for the maps from Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina of that period. So is it true that those maps you received are not from that period but of that period?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Perhaps I mis-worded myself -- or misspoke. But I -- I asked for maps that had been produced at that time. So that's my understanding that that's what was given to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What bothers me with this map is that you have enemy's -- or enemy's positions but you don't have your own positions on your own maps. Is it normal for a military map not to have your own positions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If we could just clarify the question. I don't believe Mr. Hogan has any positions on this map. Exactly what is being referred to here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I take it that you wanted to ask whether the witness considers it normal for an army to produce maps with only the -- the positions of the enemy --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The way in which you phrased it was more or less as if Mr. Hogan was a party to the conflict, which he is not, as far as I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't claim that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you answer that question, Mr. Hogan.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't have any military expertise to say whether that's normal or not. I do know that this map was seized by the OTP during a search of the ABiH archives. This was not a -- a map that was requested or produced independently. They went into the -- the team went into the archives to do a search and seized it in the year 2000.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Thank you. Now we have those text box on that map. Obviously they are glued on top of the map and then, of course, scanned and reproduced but it's visible from the -- them that you can see through them. Do you know who produced those text box? Do you have any specific knowledge?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I don't. All I know is that they were on the map when it was seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not check the accuracy of strength of troops or number of weaponry in those text box?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: You mean to compare them with the ink markings on the map, to compare the text to the ink markings on the map? No, I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't compare with any other documents whether, for example, on this -- in these text box it says that there is around 30.000 troops but only it mentioned always a bit strange title, it mentioned only, like, 500 automatic rifles, but it says: Captured and received armament and ammunition in the RgSTO. So you did not compare whether this is -- these numbers are correctly inputted on these text box?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I did not. And I'm not testifying as to the accuracy of these text boxes, just on the confrontation lines depicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you indicate where these parts you referred to are to be found on the -- on the map? And then we can zoom in on the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If I can see that. Give me one second. First, on the left side, if we can zoom -- yeah, that box. And the bottom part of the first part. Of the first part, sorry. You can see that there is, according to them, 29.295 military -- actually, soldiers. And it says that it has -- it's telling about the strength.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And then a bit further down --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this -- could I just have -- is this the left -- oh, that's the upper part of it. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Upper part. And then further down, we see "overview," and we can see English translation, if you want. It's 19961. And there is English translation as well. Of the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps we can have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 19 -- sorry, I misspoke. My mistake. 19661.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's P2951.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's the English version, which only gives the translation of the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of the boxes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- of the boxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. So there we can find on page 2 in English version, under "Captured and received armament," it says: M 41 automatic rifles, 726 millimetres, 500. So that was my -- the basis for my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, if can I assist Mr. Lukic and the Chamber. The Chamber heard evidence about the use of labels generally on the 12th -- on the 13th of November, 2012, at transcript page 4999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, totally different question although related to this. Reference is made several times to the RgSTO. Do you know what that stands for, or do the parties have any common understanding of what RgSTO stands for because it is not translated. The original and the translation are the same.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, although it's not translated, it's my understanding that it stood for Republic Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. TO often referred to Territorial Defence. And S diacritic may refer to staff. And then the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Although I'm not clear about Rg [overlapping speakers] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. If the parties could reach an agreement on that, that would assist the Chamber in understanding it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just have a question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You talked earlier when you started asking questions to Mr. Hogan about the -- this -- these writings, you said this represents the numerical strength. I see this is titled: "Captured and received armament and ammunition." Or -- or am I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What puzzles me is "received."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, that puzzles me too. I don't know, received from whom. But "captured," I would have thought this is just mentioning what was captured not what is the full strength either of themselves or the enemy, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Exactly. If it's common understanding, then we wouldn't have a problem if it is just captured. Only I asked the gentleman if he checked whether it stands for the whole armament they had or just captured that's -- but the gentleman told us, Mr. Hogan told us that he never checked those numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think the focus of Mr. Hogan was on confrontation lines rather than on the presence of troops or equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when using this particular map we should be -- actually have that in mind, that those text boxes were not established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, they are established but not yet explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or -- explained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I consult with Mr. Mladic for one minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you can. If it's urgent. Otherwise, it could be done at the end of your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, volume such that no one can hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I apologise for this, Mr. Hogan. Next, you told us about elevations, and you marked some elevations around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So if we can have this map, which is now P2951, on our screens but zoomed out. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way - and sorry to interrupt - I see that on the first page of the English text, there -- just before the total, the RgSTO is -- the acronym is presented as Regional Territorial Defence Staff. Now I know that, Mr. Lukic, that the Defence has sometimes complained about acronyms being interpreted by the translators, but here it may assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So that was our understanding too, that it's regional Rg, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hogan, you talked --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we can have this map on the full screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You talked about elevations in the hands of AB and H, and you mentioned Colina Kapa, Debelo Brdo, Zuc, and Hum. Do you know where hill Vranjace is? And I can tell that you it is near to Debelo Brdo. Vranjace.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Grdonj is, also in the hands of Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it on this map?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the central area. Grdonj is approximately here. Shall I put a G next to it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would ask for this marking to be introduced into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document receives number D439, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. The markings, at the request of the Defence, are in blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where Balino Brdo?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Balino Brdo, I believe it's in the same region as Zuc but I'm not 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know that AB and H could control Vogosca from there.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it on this map.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I would have to have it zoomed in where I could not read the inscriptions. I can give it an approximation but it's very --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, just approximately.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: -- broad approximation. It would be in that general area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm a bit puzzled by what happens now. The witness is asked whether he knows certain location. Then he says it's somewhere near Zuc. Then, Mr. Lukic, you give him additional information. The witness then says that's possible, true or not. And then you asked him to mark it on the map, which is a bit of a strange way of -- but -- Mr. Hogan, what you now marked, is that approximately where you remember Balino Brdo to be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's approximate, Your Honour. But an examination of the maps with the labels would be able to -- the parties would be able to see it on these maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean to say also that it is irrespective of what Mr. Lukic told you about this location.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand. Yes, this location is where I recall in the general area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's fine. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this area -- actually, it's obviously under the control of B and H, right? It's inside the red circle?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And do you know where Brijesce Brdo is?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you mark it on the same map, please.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Perhaps I should put BR next to Brijesce.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And -- maybe BB.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: BB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Looks more like a D, Mr. Hogan. The second one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, I would ask for this to be saved, maybe instead of the first one, since here we have both markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If it is possible to be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can -- let me just see. This will be -- you said instead of the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Instead of D439. D439 has only markings for the first hill. Now on this one we have both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we vacate the other one and replace it by this map now marked by the witness with the markings BB for Balino Brdo and BR for Brijesce Brdo. Yes, please proceed. And, Madam Registrar, could you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is then now D439.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This needs some administrative attention. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This elevation is also inside the circle of the Army of B and H.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can we zoom out now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this map, can you mark mountain Igman.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Igman ran roughly ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Igman was under control of Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina since when?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Um --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or till when, if you know?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I know it was taken by the SRK, I think, in 1993, but under a UN agreement, they -- they turned it back over. So I -- I would say, other than a short period of a few months, it was under the control of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I would offer this marking into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I -- I have no problems in it being admitted into evidence. But you said it was later under the control of the UN. That is excluded then from -- you said it was only for a few months --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, under an agreement with the UN, the SRK gave it back or vacated their positions on Igman and the ABiH moved back into their positions, their own positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think we heard evidence about the -- the regime that was then imposed and whether or not it was violated. Madam Registrar, the number for this map again marked by the witness with Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be number D440, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D440 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would need P2952. Also, it's the other map used today.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You marked several of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe it's better to have P2959. Can we have 8, please. Sorry, I -- P2958. Yes, that's -- that's the map we need.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, you marked airport settlement. And, of course, you just drew a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the usher to help us to distribute this map. I will give it to Mr. Hogan, Their Honours, and the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This map was used in Galic trial. It was P3732 in Galic case. And map was marked by Mr. Ismet Hadzic. Do you know, Mr. Hogan, that Mr. Ismet Hadzic was commander of Dobrinja Brigade?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I do know that. He was the commander until he was wounded and taken out of action, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On this map, it is visible that part of airport settlement is still in the hands of Army of B and H, and I think that you presented it on your drawing, correct me if I'm wrong, but is it true that part of airport settlement was in the hands of Army of B and H?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if we're talking about the same term here. The airport settlement that I understand is always referred to as airport settlement is the area in the -- horizontally in the centre along the left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you think it's not presented -- maybe I'm wrong. You think it's not presented on this map.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: The airport settlement is visible. What I call the airport settlement --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- first of all, could we have this on the ELMO so that we can -- it becomes part of the -- if there's any extra copy. Because I first want to know exactly what appears to depict the confrontation line here. What exactly is understood by the airport settlement ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could use the pointer to explain what I understand as the airport settlement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, could we, first of all -- first of all, could we -- it has been presented to us, but 90 degrees turned clockwise. Yes? That is how it is presented, and that's -- now we can read the text. What I see and just -- I'd like to explore whether that is any marking depicting a confrontation line, that is, coming from approximately the middle of the top side where there seems to be a marking of a small number 1 in a small circle. If we take it from there, we see in this black-and-white picture a grey line, starting to turn slightly to the left, which, I take it, is west. Then going around what seems to be two built-up structures, crossing what I think I remember is the Dobrinja river canalised in the middle of Dobrinja, going further south, then going up to north-west again rather sharply, then turning down. Is that -- what I describe here, is that in your understanding, Mr. Hogan, the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Your Honour, as drawn by Mr. Hadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we see is that we follow this confrontation line further to the south, that it reaches a built-up area with a half-circled shape in its entirety, and it seems that the confrontation line runs through that built-up structure but only marginally to the southeastern side, leaving 95 per cent of the settlement on the ABiH -- on the -- on the Serb side. Now, we see two similarly shaped structures. That is almost in half a circle existing of what seems to be various large number of apartment buildings. Mr. Hogan, when you refer to the airport settlement, did you refer to the one more to the left upper side, more to the northwestern side, or did you refer to the slightly different, although basically the same shape which is found a little bit to the south-east?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was referring to the structure to the north-west, the furthest left as we view this image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the one where on this sketch the confrontation line just -- is just inside the southeastern portion, although a very limited portion, of that settlement.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I tried to organise things in such way that we know what we are talking about. Please put your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As it -- first, I need instruction from the Registry. Is it possible to save image from the ELMO? So we just can just ask Mr. Hogan to mark --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we could ask the witness to do is to mark the hard copy on the ELMO, and then the marked copy could be given to the Registry and could be uploaded ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the technicalities are still to be discussed. But once the witness has marked on the ELMO, then through, under the control of the Registry, it will be -- later be uploaded and provisionally a number can already be assigned to the then-marked copy. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hogan, just for -- would you be so kind and mark airport settlement on this map.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And would you be so kind and mark confrontation line, just part of it, because Judge Orie already explained.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just put CL.

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if we can provisionally assign the number for this sketch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you reserve a number for this document marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Hard copy marked by the witness receives number D441, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we'll have to wait until it's uploaded. Do you need this any further, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, we don't, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could the usher give it to the Registrar. Whatever has to be done by the parties later should be under the supervision and control of the Registry because it's now marked by the witness and is in progress of being -- of becoming an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, when you asked B and H -- Army of B and H to provide you with maps, and we saw that they draw Serbian positions and Serbian armament, have you ever received maps from them with inputted positions of Army of B and H?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, on this map here there are positions of the Army of BiH. Weapons positions, I should say.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On -- it's -- when you say on this one, you mean P2952?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If the Prosecution can confirm that when Mr. Hogan said "on this map," he meant P2952, which is map in front of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which is what we see, the big one we see behind the witness. That's the correct number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we ask the witness to -- perhaps to have P2952 on our screens and explain to us, either on the screen or to start with on the large map, where the BiH military positions are depicted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we have P2952 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we could zoom it in towards the central area. That should be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps to cut matters short -- no. I let you -- please explain to us, Mr. Hogan, where you see the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the area of Zuc, for example, if I could mark on this map, there is a weapons position here. Weapons position here. Over in Brijesce Brdo there's a weapons position there. And here. And, again, marked in ink that are much more visible when it's zoomed in further or -- or seeing it in the full-size map. But they're dark blue ink which tends to blend in a little bit with the background -- the natural background of the map. So they're a little bit harder to see on this map than other maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that, do we also see depicted here areas where a certain unit was deployed. I see, for example, on that same Zuc hill, 1112, and then what seems to be a reference to some kind of a brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, those are the units that were -- had the zone of responsibility there, but their headquarters positions were not marked on this map. There are other maps from the ABiH where such buildings are marked but not this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So this is limited to weapon positions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Generally some weapons positions and the zones of responsibility of the brigades. And battalions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I take it that you also have not verified whether these markings are complete reflections of weapon positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not verified. And I should point out that a depiction such as this and on the other maps that showed the SRK positions, they have -- the images have to be -- or the symbols, sorry, the symbols have to be outsized. So, for example, an image symbol showing a cannon, if the -- an actual cannon was that size on the ground as is depicted on the map, it would be immense. So an image that is -- a symbol that is shown on a map gives a general area not a precise location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I guess, since you said you didn't check exactly that here on that list, we saw in English, it's -- it only says 56 Howitzers or mortars 120-millimetre, 97 pieces, obviously would you agree with me that not everything was marked on this map?

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: I can't --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can't --

utterances.speaker: BARRY HOGAN [Recalled]
utterances.text: -- either confirm or deny --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just to clarify you were referring to the other map now?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, I'm referring to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where did you take these numbers from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where did you take number 56 from, for example?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is even from 1992. I guess there must be only more weaponry in ABiH position than in 1992 although this map is from 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But where did you read 56?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's from -- it has P number now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now are you referring to the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, yes, to the other map. It's P2951 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They are from different time periods.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is -- yes, I see you are relying on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Previous period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the previous text boxes --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the text boxes we saw which were unexplained --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- what they were. Yes. Okay. Then you'd say --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But the witness said he didn't check so we will have to establish it with somebody else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And I'm actually finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'll have to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Hogan, I just want to thank you for answering to our questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you tender this marked map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The map marked by the witness, Madam Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The map as marked by the witness receives number D442, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Similarly, as with the other map, the Chamber would like to have a look at this map out of the courtroom, the original, so as to be better able to see what the markings exactly are.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: With respect to D442, Your Honour, I think it would be important that I would state on the record that I have checked the Galic judgement and I do verify that it is the map done by Mr. Ismet Hadzic and it was Exhibit P3732 in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
